rules.name: Windows event log cleared

context.summary: Clearing the Security (1102) or System (104) log removes evidence of earlier activity. Attackers do this after privilege escalation or before ransomware.
falsePositives: Documented log maintenance by an administrator
Imaging or re-provisioning of a lab machine
maliciousIndicators: Cleared by an account that is not a log-management admin
Cleared shortly after other findings on the same host
Cleared outside a change window

investigate.title: Check who cleared the log and when
Look for the same host in your SIEM before the clear time
investigate.command: SecurityEvent | where Computer == "{{computer}}" | order by TimeGenerated desc

remediate.title: Isolate the host (EDR or network quarantine) pending triage
remediate.command: Use your EDR / NAC to isolate {{computer}}.

remediate.title: Preserve the remaining logs before more are lost
remediate.command: $h='{{computer}}'; wevtutil epl Security "C:\IR\Security-$h.evtx"

rules.name: Audit policy changed

context.summary: Weakening audit policy reduces what future attacks will record.
falsePositives: Group Policy refresh applying a legitimate baseline
Security hardening projects
maliciousIndicators: Audit categories set to 'No Auditing'
Change made by a non-admin or service account

investigate.title: Review the effective audit policy

remediate.title: Reapply the baseline audit policy via Group Policy
remediate.command: gpupdate /force on {{computer}} after confirming the GPO is correct.

rules.name: Repeated failed logons against one account from one source (brute force)

context.summary: Ten or more failed logons for the same account from the same address within five minutes suggests password guessing.
falsePositives: A user or service with an expired or stale saved password
Misconfigured scheduled task or mapped drive
maliciousIndicators: External or unusual source IP
A successful 4624 for the same account right after the burst
Many different accounts targeted from the same IP (see AUTH-002)

investigate.title: Did the account later log on successfully from this source?
investigate.command: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4624 and TargetUserName == "{{targetUserName}}" and IpAddress == "{{ipAddress}}"

remediate.title: Block the source IP at the perimeter
remediate.command: Block {{ipAddress}} on the firewall / WAF after confirming it is not internal infrastructure.

remediate.title: Force a password reset if a success followed
remediate.command: Reset the password for {{targetUserName}} and revoke active sessions.

rules.name: One source failing logons across many accounts (password spraying)

context.summary: A single source failing logons against ten or more distinct accounts in 30 minutes is characteristic of password spraying.
falsePositives: A shared NAT / proxy IP in front of many legitimate users
Vulnerability scanners or pen-test activity
maliciousIndicators: Common passwords tried across the whole directory
Source IP is external or a known-bad address
Any account that then succeeds from the same IP

investigate.title: List accounts that succeeded from this source
investigate.command: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4624 and IpAddress == "{{ipAddress}}" | summarize count() by TargetUserName

remediate.title: Block the source IP
remediate.command: Block {{ipAddress}} and review any account it authenticated to.

rules.name: Logon with explicit credentials

context.summary: A process used different credentials than the logged-on user (runas, mapped drives, lateral tooling).
falsePositives: Interactive 'Run as different user'
Scheduled tasks and service accounts
Outlook / SMB clients using saved credentials
maliciousIndicators: Initiated by an unusual process
Target server is a domain controller or file server the user never uses

rules.name: Network or RDP logon from a non-private IPv4 address

context.summary: A successful network/RDP logon whose source is a public IPv4 address means a remote service is reachable from the internet. IPv6 sources are not evaluated.
falsePositives: Intentionally internet-facing RDP gateways or VPN concentrators
Remote staff on a corporate VPN that presents public egress IPs
maliciousIndicators: Source geolocates outside your normal footprint
Preceded by failed logons (AUTH-001/002)
Followed by privileged activity or new processes

investigate.title: Review all logons from this source
investigate.command: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4624 and IpAddress == "{{ipAddress}}" | project TimeGenerated, Computer, TargetUserName, LogonType

remediate.title: Restrict RDP exposure
remediate.command: Remove direct internet exposure for {{computer}}; require VPN/RD Gateway with MFA.

rules.name: NTLM network logon by a user account (pass-the-hash indicator)

context.summary: Type 3 NTLM logons with a user account can indicate pass-the-hash, but NTLM is still common in many networks. Treat as context for other findings, not a verdict.
falsePositives: Legacy applications and IP-based SMB access
File servers accessed by IP address
maliciousIndicators: Admin account authenticating to many hosts in a short time
Workstation-to-workstation NTLM

rules.name: Special privileges assigned to a non-system account

context.summary: An admin-level logon occurred. Normal for administrators; valuable as a link in correlated chains (Phase 3).
falsePositives: Every logon by a member of Administrators

rules.name: New service installed

context.summary: Services run as SYSTEM and survive reboots, so attackers use them for persistence and remote execution (PsExec-style).
falsePositives: Software installs and updates
Endpoint agent deployments
maliciousIndicators: Binary in a temp/user-writable path
Random service name
Service created over the network by an admin account

investigate.title: Inspect the service binary path

remediate.title: Stop and remove a confirmed-malicious service
remediate.command: $h='{{computer}}'; $s='{{serviceName}}'; sc.exe \\$h stop $s; sc.exe \\$h delete $s

rules.name: Scheduled task created

context.summary: Scheduled tasks provide persistence and delayed or remote execution.
falsePositives: Software updaters and management tooling
Admin-created maintenance jobs
maliciousIndicators: Task runs a script from a user-writable path
Task created by a remote logon
Randomized task name

investigate.title: List scheduled tasks on the host

rules.name: User account created

context.summary: New accounts are a common persistence mechanism.
falsePositives: HR on-boarding automation
Helpdesk-created accounts
maliciousIndicators: Created outside business hours
Creator is not an identity-management account
Immediately added to a privileged group (ACC-002)

investigate.title: Review the new account

remediate.title: Disable the account if unauthorized
remediate.command: Disable-ADAccount -Identity '{{targetUserName}}'

rules.name: Member added to a privileged group

context.summary: For 4728/4732/4756 the target name is the group. Additions to administrative groups grant broad access.
falsePositives: Approved joiner/mover/leaver admin changes
Software installers adding service accounts to local Administrators
maliciousIndicators: Change made by a non-admin or compromised account
No matching change ticket
Account added was created recently (ACC-001)

investigate.title: List current members of the group

remediate.title: Disable the account pending review
remediate.command: Disable-ADAccount -Identity '{{subjectUserName}}'

rules.name: Suspicious PowerShell command line

context.summary: Encoded commands, in-memory download cradles and hidden windows are staples of malicious PowerShell.
falsePositives: Configuration management (SCCM, Intune, Ansible) and RMM tools
Admin automation using encoded commands
maliciousIndicators: Parent is Office, a browser, or a script host
Decoded payload downloads or injects code
Run by a user who does not normally use PowerShell

investigate.title: Decode a base64 payload from the command line
Hunt this host's recent process creations

remediate.title: Isolate the host (EDR or network quarantine) pending triage
remediate.command: Use your EDR / NAC to isolate {{computer}}.

remediate.title: Disable the account pending review
remediate.command: Disable-ADAccount -Identity '{{subjectUserName}}'

rules.name: Living-off-the-land binary abuse

context.summary: Signed Windows binaries used to download or execute payloads while avoiding application allow-listing.
falsePositives: certutil used to manage certificates (without -urlcache)
Software deployment scripts using bitsadmin
maliciousIndicators: Remote URL pointing to a raw IP or newly registered domain
Output written to a temp or user directory

investigate.title: Hunt this host's recent process creations

remediate.title: Isolate the host (EDR or network quarantine) pending triage
remediate.command: Use your EDR / NAC to isolate {{computer}}.

rules.name: Office application spawned a command interpreter

context.summary: Office should not normally launch shells or script hosts. This is the classic malicious-document pattern. Requires 4688 events that include ParentProcessName (Windows 10 / Server 2016+).
falsePositives: Legitimate macros or add-ins that call cmd.exe
Line-of-business Excel workbooks automating tools
maliciousIndicators: Document recently downloaded or emailed
Child process makes network connections or downloads files

investigate.title: Hunt this host's recent process creations

remediate.title: Isolate the host (EDR or network quarantine) pending triage
remediate.command: Use your EDR / NAC to isolate {{computer}}.

rules.name: Credential dumping tool or technique

context.summary: Command lines that dump LSASS memory, SAM/SECURITY hives or the AD database give attackers reusable credentials.
falsePositives: Authorized red-team / pen-test activity
Crash-dump collection by a documented debugging process
maliciousIndicators: Executed by a non-admin or unexpected account
Dump file written to a temp path and then copied off-host

investigate.title: Hunt this host's recent process creations

remediate.title: Isolate the host (EDR or network quarantine) pending triage
remediate.command: Use your EDR / NAC to isolate {{computer}}.

remediate.title: Reset credentials of every account that logged on to the host
remediate.command: Treat all accounts with sessions on {{computer}} as compromised; reset and rotate KRBTGT if a DC is involved.

rules.name: Many service tickets requested by one account (Kerberoasting heuristic)

context.summary: Requesting tickets for many distinct service accounts quickly can be offline password cracking prep. This rule does not see ticket encryption type; check for RC4 (0x17) in the raw events.
falsePositives: Admin tools and monitoring that enumerate SPNs
Application servers touching many services at startup
maliciousIndicators: RC4 (0x17) ticket encryption
Requests from a workstation not used for admin work

rules.name: Account and group discovery commands

context.summary: Reconnaissance of privileged groups and domain structure usually follows initial access.
falsePositives: Administrators troubleshooting access
Inventory and audit scripts
maliciousIndicators: Several discovery commands in quick succession
Run from a user or service account that is not an admin

rules.name: Security tooling or logging tampering command

context.summary: Commands that disable antivirus, firewall or logging are used to hide later stages of an attack.
falsePositives: Authorized AV exclusion requests
Software installers that temporarily stop security services
maliciousIndicators: Executed by a non-admin or remote session
Followed by suspicious process activity

investigate.title: Hunt this host's recent process creations

remediate.title: Isolate the host (EDR or network quarantine) pending triage
remediate.command: Use your EDR / NAC to isolate {{computer}}.

rules.name: Backup or shadow copy destruction (ransomware precursor)

context.summary: Deleting shadow copies and backup catalogs prevents recovery and is among the most reliable ransomware signals.
falsePositives: Rare: storage-pressure maintenance scripts run by admins
maliciousIndicators: Occurs minutes before mass file modification
Executed from a remote session or a script in a temp path

investigate.title: Check for encrypted-file activity on the host
investigate.command: Look for rapid file renames/extension changes on {{computer}} and notify the incident commander immediately.

remediate.title: Isolate the host (EDR or network quarantine) pending triage
remediate.command: Use your EDR / NAC to isolate {{computer}}.

rules.name: Network logon, special privileges, then encoded PowerShell in the same session

context.summary: Linked by Logon ID across 4624, 4672 and 4688. A remote logon that gets admin privileges and immediately runs encoded PowerShell is a common lateral-movement pattern.
falsePositives: Configuration management and approved admin automation

rules.name: Successful logon after repeated failures from the same source (brute-force success)

context.summary: Five or more failed logons for an account from one address, followed by a success for the same account from that address, means the guessing may have worked.
falsePositives: A user who mistyped a password repeatedly and then succeeded
Stale credentials in a service that eventually refreshed
maliciousIndicators: External source IP
Success is followed by privileged activity or new processes
Account is an administrator or service account

investigate.title: Review everything this account did after the success
investigate.command: SecurityEvent | where TargetUserName == "{{targetUserName}}" or SubjectUserName == "{{targetUserName}}" | order by TimeGenerated asc

remediate.title: Reset the password and revoke sessions
remediate.command: Reset the password for {{targetUserName}}, revoke refresh tokens/sessions, and review MFA.

rules.name: New account created and added to a privileged group

context.summary: An account created and immediately given administrative group membership is a classic persistence step.
falsePositives: Approved break-glass or admin account provisioning
maliciousIndicators: No matching change ticket
Created and promoted by the same non-admin account
Account name mimics a service or built-in account

investigate.title: Check who created and promoted the account
investigate.command: SecurityEvent | where EventID in (4720, 4728, 4732, 4756) | where TargetUserName == "{{targetUserName}}" or MemberName has "{{targetUserName}}"

remediate.title: Disable the new account
remediate.command: Disable-ADAccount -Identity '{{targetUserName}}'

rules.name: Service installed from a remote logon session (PsExec-style execution)

context.summary: A network logon whose session installs a service within minutes is how PsExec and similar tools run code on a remote host.
falsePositives: Software deployment tools and remote admin sessions
maliciousIndicators: Service binary in a temp or ADMIN$ path
Random service name
Source host is a workstation, not a management server

investigate.title: Inspect the installed service

remediate.title: Isolate the host (EDR or network quarantine) pending triage
remediate.command: Use your EDR / NAC to isolate {{computer}}.

rules.name: Privileged session cleared the audit log

context.summary: The same logon session that received special privileges then cleared the Security log, tying the clear to a specific account and session.
falsePositives: Documented log maintenance by an administrator
maliciousIndicators: Session started remotely (see logon type)
Other findings on the same host shortly before the clear

remediate.title: Isolate the host (EDR or network quarantine) pending triage
remediate.command: Use your EDR / NAC to isolate {{computer}}.
